metadata.title: Manetho — AI-powered cultural heritage platform
metadata.description: Read hieroglyphs, explore museums, and learn about Ancient Egypt with a transparent AI assistant.
metadata.keywords: Egyptology, hieroglyphs, museums, translation, AI, Ancient Egypt

home.title: Read the writing. See the objects. Understand the world.
home.subtitle: Manetho recognises hieroglyphs, translates inscriptions, and guides you through museum collections — showing its confidence, citing its sources, and never inventing an answer.
home.heroNote: Upload a photo or pick a sample inscription. Every result shows per-sign confidence and cites its sources.
home.featuresSubtitle: AI that shows its work, from the sign it is least sure about to the book it learned from.

features.signsBody: Every sign carries its Gardiner code, Unicode value and phonetic values — sourced from the Unicode Egyptian Hieroglyphs block and Gardiner's sign list.
features.confidenceBody: When Manetho is unsure, it says so. Uncertain readings are marked, not hidden, and never presented as fact.
features.sourcesBody: The assistant distinguishes established fact from interpretation and cites the standard literature it relies on.
features.assistantBody: Ask about an artifact you're looking at, an inscription you just scanned, or a tour stop. The assistant knows where you are.
features.museumBody: Interactive floor plans with object locations, curated tours, and augmented reality for supported objects.
features.learningBody: Ten structured lessons from the 24 consonant signs to reading a real offering formula, with quizzes that explain their answers.

home.howSubtitle: Three steps from a photograph to a readable translation.

howSteps.oneBody: Photograph an inscription, or choose one of the sample texts. Nothing leaves your device without your say-so.
howSteps.twoBody: The vision pass locates each sign, then the OCR pass refines the reading against the sign database.
howSteps.threeBody: You get a transliteration, a translation, alternative readings, grammar notes, historical context and cited sources.

home.featuredSubtitle: Start with a few well-documented pieces from the collection.
home.museumsSubtitle: Explore four collections, from Giza to London.
home.ctaBody: Start with a sample inscription — no camera needed.

translate.title: Translate an inscription
translate.subtitle: Upload a photograph or choose a sample. The reading shows per-sign confidence and cites its sources.
translate.dropzone: Drop an image here, or click to choose a file
translate.dropzoneHint: PNG or JPEG up to 10 MB. Clear, well-lit, straight-on photos work best.
translate.sampleNote: Samples are synthetic images generated for demonstration.
translate.noAlternatives: No alternative readings were produced for this text.
translate.cropHint: Drag to select just the inscription. A tighter crop usually improves the reading.
translate.manuallySelectHint: No confident reading? Choose the signs yourself from the database and Manetho will transliterate them.
translate.disclaimer: Computer-assisted recognition. A confident reading is not a substitute for expert Egyptological work.
translate.failureTitle: We couldn't confidently read this inscription.
translate.failureBody: The signs could not be identified with enough confidence to offer a translation. Rather than guess, Manetho stops here.
translate.failureHints: You can improve the result by:
translate.failureHint1: photographing the inscription straight-on in even, bright light
translate.failureHint2: cropping tightly to the inscription itself
translate.failureHint3: avoiding glare, shadows and heavy perspective distortion
translate.failureHint4: choosing the signs manually from the sign database
translate.lowConfidenceBody: We read some signs, but not with enough confidence to give a translation. Here is what we detected so you can check it.
translate.demoProviderNotice: Demo mode: readings come from a deterministic local provider, not a trained vision model.

assistant.disclaimer: The assistant distinguishes established fact from interpretation and cites its sources. When it doesn't know, it says so.
